To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of cytoreductive surgeries has decreased over time, but the number of patients undergoing cytoreductive surgery has increased, and that the number of patients with a solitary kidney undergoing cytoreductive nephrec-tomy is also increasing.

the use of cytotoxic chemotherapy for the treatment of metastatic renal cell carcinoma increased in the United States between 1992 and 2005, with the greatest increase observed in the use of interleukin-2 and interferon-alfa.

the number of patients who received cytoreductive nephrec- tomy (CRN) decreased over time, and that the proportion of patients who received CRN decreased over time for patients with clear cell carcinoma (CC) but not for patients with papillary or chromophobe renal cell carcinoma (RCC).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of cytotoxic chemotherapy in the treatment of patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma.
the use of cytotoxic drugs in the treatment of cancer.
the development and implementation of a new method of treatment of renal cell carcinoma (RCC).

the use of cytotoxic chemotherapy in the treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma has been shown to be effective in prolonging survival and improving quality of life in a small percentage of patients.
there is insufficient evidence to support a role for cytoreductive nephroureterectomy in the primary treatment of patients with upper tract urothelial carcinoma.
the use of cytotoxic chemotherapy for patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma has been disappointing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the use of cytodestructive nephrectomy has been increasing in the USA.
the use of cytodeuctive nephrectomy has been declining in the United States, and the decline appears to be accelerating.
we found that the use of cytotoxicity nephrectomy has decreased over time, with the most important decrease occurring among patients with metastases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of cytotoxic chemotherapy in patients with metastatic RCC is increasing and that the use of CNI in the adjuvant setting is decreasing, while the use of adjuvant immunotherapy is increasing.
the incidence of renal cell carcinoma is increasing, and that this is due to an increase in the incidence of non-clear cell renal cell carcinoma, particularly papillary renal cell carcinoma.
there is no clear benefit for patients undergoing nephrectomy.
